content:
nina: FYI we got a support ticket from beta-customer about unexpected extra provisional charges during a streaming session where the client truncated the response mid-toolcall.

sam: Huh. Truncation + toolcall combo? Can you paste the snippet they sent (logs + payloads)?

nina: pasted anonymized logs below. client did an explicit close after 2 tokens because UX timed out, server later retried the toolcall and a provisional charge was generated again. trace=tik-77

```
[2025-06-02T09:12:01Z] stream.recv session=ses-900 req_id=req-33 partial=true truncated_by_client=true
[2025-06-02T09:12:01Z] toolcall.start id=tc-451 invocation_id=inv-77 provisional_issue id=pv-200 src=stream
[2025-06-02T09:12:02Z] stream.close client_closed=true
[2025-06-02T09:12:03Z] retry-scheduler queued toolcall inv-77 retry_reason=early_eof
[2025-06-02T09:12:03Z] toolcall.start id=tc-452 invocation_id=inv-77 provisional_issue id=pv-201 src=retry
[2025-06-02T09:12:04Z] toolcall.confirm id=tc-452 confirmed_tokens=320
```

carla: So the same invocation_id was retried but the ledger treated pv-200 and pv-201 as separate. Double provisional was visible until one was confirmed, but the customer saw the provisional spike and panicked.

leo: Do we currently dedupe provisional by invocation_id? I thought provisional_id is unique and we only reconcile later.

sam: Ledger dedupe key is provisional_id. invocation_id is not strictly enforced because some legacy toolcalls didn't populate it. We do have an optional invocation_fingerprint but most callers don't set it.

nina: Client side truncated and closed; our retry scheduler re-enqueued the toolcall with same invocation_id, but created a new provisional entry. That's the double-charge.

leo: Short-term: detect truncated_by_client events and suppress automatic retry for the same invocation_id for N seconds. Add metric `toolcall_truncate_retry_suppressed`.

carla: Console change: surface `truncated_by_client` as a column on request detail and include a quick "mark provisional as stale" button for ops. That reduces support overhead.

sam: Longer-term: ledger should be idempotent on (invocation_id, session_id) when invocation_id is present. If invocation_id missing, fall back to current behavior but emit a high-cardinality debug tag so we can find callers that need to set invocation_id.

marta: For rollout we need shadow mode. Implement dedupe in ledger but run in shadow: emit header `x-dedupe-decision` with values {shadow_duplicate, shadow_new}. No billing change until we flip.

ops-bot: Runbook note created: runbook/toolcall/dedupe-truncate-quirk. Owner: leo. ETA 48h.

leo: I'll add a dashboard card: top 10 invocation_ids by provisional_dup_count and a realtime gauge `toolcall_truncate_dup_rate` by route/region.

carla: UX note: the refund CTA should pre-populate time window and invocation_id. Also add a tooltip explaining why provisional may be higher than confirmed.

sam: Action items: 1) sam + leo implement ledger shadow dedupe PR 2) leo add probe metrics + dashboard 3) carla add console columns + refund CTA 4) nina coordinate support message and customer hold-off on refunds 5) marta approve canary plan.

marta: Approving canary: 2% traffic shadow for 6 hours, if shadow_duplicate ratio <0.2% and no data inconsistencies then schedule progressive rollout.

sam: Also require tests for callers that omit invocation_id: ensure we log candidate keys so we can prod clients to upgrade.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2025-087 created: "toolcall double provisional on client truncate". Linked to runbook and this thread.

nina: I'll send the support note to beta-customer explaining we're shadowing a fix and will follow up with reconciliation if we find erroneous provisional charges. Thanks all :heart:
